options: A fully managed hybrid search service for unstructured text, used for retrieval in RAG pipelines
A self-hosted vector database you must install and tune manually
A replacement for all Snowflake tables
A tool exclusively for translating between languages
questions.explain: Cortex Search is fully managed by Snowflake and combines multiple retrieval methods for unstructured text.

questions.q: Why is Cortex Search described as 'hybrid'?
options: It runs vector search, keyword search, and semantic reranking together on every query
It only works with a hybrid of two Snowflake accounts at once
It mixes structured and unstructured storage formats on disk
It alternates randomly between search methods on each call
questions.explain: Every query runs vector, keyword, and semantic reranking passes together, blending the strengths of each without manual weight tuning.

questions.q: What does TARGET_LAG control when creating a Cortex Search service?
options: How fresh the search index stays relative to the underlying source table
The maximum number of search results returned
The geographic region where the service is hosted
The warehouse size used to run the query
questions.explain: TARGET_LAG governs index freshness, refreshed automatically by Snowflake, similar to how a Dynamic Table manages its own refresh schedule.

questions.q: In the RAG pipeline described in this lesson, what role does Cortex Search play relative to AI_COMPLETE?
options: Cortex Search retrieves relevant document chunks first; those chunks are then included in the prompt sent to AI_COMPLETE
AI_COMPLETE runs first and Cortex Search only summarizes its output afterward
They are unrelated and never used together
Cortex Search replaces AI_COMPLETE entirely, with no LLM call needed
questions.explain: Retrieval happens first — Cortex Search finds relevant chunks, which are stitched into a prompt that AI_COMPLETE then answers, grounding the response in real documents.

questions.q: What embedding model powers the vector-search component of Cortex Search by default?
options: Arctic Embed, Snowflake's own embedding model (with support for bringing a custom embedding model as of March 2026)
A third-party model that must be purchased and installed separately
No embedding model is used — Cortex Search is keyword-only
A model that must be trained from scratch by the customer before first use
questions.explain: Snowflake's Arctic Embed model powers vector search by default; as of March 2026, customers can also bring their own pre-computed or fine-tuned embeddings.
